title: AI research without the Hermes/OpenClaw nonsense
author: SnowSilent7695
selftext:
Saw a few posts about using a Hermes agent for investing, since it can constantly run in the background, spawn subsequent jobs, delegate tasks to other agents, etc. While I initially loved the idea, it's a nightmare to setup and manage, making wide-scale adoption a pipe-dream (I remember OpenClaw being buzzy for about 2-3 weeks and then falling off a cliff). And more importantly, they're just the wrong tool for this kind of thing (you're asking it to be both a data pipeline and a trader).

  
I've always wanted to just spin up Claude, have it constantly listen to the market, taking everything in, thinking about it, and bringing a few ideas to me throughout the day that normally wouldn't cross my radar. And finally wanted to share a live demo of this happening, asking Claude, "lookout for the biggest movers, earnings releases, transcript updates, investor decks, and 8K releases post market close." I'll note that Claude is just listening for these new updates; it's not scraping the web, looking for new SEC filings, etc., making it a clean separation of concerns, cost-effective and accessible.

comments.author: SnowSilent7695
comments.body:
Anyone is welcome to try the workflow in Claude through its connectors: add custom connection > in remote server url [https://mcp.flexreportfinapi.com/mcp](https://mcp.flexreportfinapi.com/mcp)

The codebase for the workflow is also public, which also highlights other use-cases and allows you to modify it and make it your own: [https://github.com/cbecks1212/flexreport-mcp](https://github.com/cbecks1212/flexreport-mcp)

comments.author: leroylabs
comments.body: The screenshot's “Reconnected to flexreport” line raises a useful test: disconnect Claude around an after-hours earnings release, then reconnect after the associated 8-K arrives. Does it receive both missed events once, with their original publication times, or only updates arriving after reconnection? Separating the feed from Claude makes sense, but a silent gap could leave it discussing the earnings release without the filing. How does Flexreport handle catching up after a disconnect?

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: agree on the split. an agent that has to fetch its own data burns most of its tokens on plumbing and still misses the filing. feed it events and let it do the thinking.
